Garrulous

GAIR-uh-lus · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Garrulous is excessively talkative, especially about unimportant matters, in a rambling way.

The garrulous neighbor kept the mail carrier on the porch for twenty minutes every single day.

Worked Example

Once the garrulous barber started talking, customers knew their haircut would take twice as long as anywhere else in town.

Garrulous describes talkativeness that rambles on past the point anyone wants to keep listening.

How Garrulous Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

chatty

chatty: talkative in a casual, friendly way

rambling

rambling: wandering on without a clear point

Antonyms

taciturn

taciturn: reluctant to speak much

reticent

reticent: reserved and uncommunicative

How Strong Is It? — talkative → garrulous → loquacious

talkative vs. garrulous

talkative vs. garrulous: Talkative is a plain, everyday word for liking to talk; garrulous adds a tiresome, rambling quality that can wear on a listener.

loquacious vs. garrulous

loquacious vs. garrulous: Loquacious describes fluent, often skillful talkativeness, while garrulous leans toward aimless, tiresome chatter.

Sort It Out

Build the Word

The pieces

root — garr

root — garr: to chatter (Latin (garrire, imitative))

suffix — -ulous

suffix — -ulous: full of, inclined to (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: garr- ('to chatter') + -ulous ('full of') together give the sense of chattering excessively.

Use the root in a new word: garrulity

Use the root in a new word: garrulity: Garrulity is the noun form of the same word family, naming excessive talkativeness itself -- not an independent new root.
